# Cyclotomic polynomials

## Primitive Roots of Unity

The n-th cyclotomic polynomial has the primitive n-th roots of unity as its roots.

Its degree is Euler phi of n.

The polynomial is irreducible over the rational numbers.

## Factoring x^n minus one

The polynomial x to the n minus one factors into cyclotomic polynomials indexed by the divisors of n.

The degrees of those factors add up to n.

For a prime p the cyclotomic polynomial is a geometric series with p terms.

## Extensions Generated by a Root

A primitive root generates an extension whose degree is the order of the multiplicative group modulo n.

That order is phi of n, matching the degree of the polynomial.

The same count answers both the polynomial question and the field extension question.

A cyclotomic question usually reduces to Euler phi. Compute phi by factoring n into prime powers and multiplying n by one minus the reciprocal of each prime. That value is the degree of the polynomial and the degree of the extension.

For example, phi of 12 is 4 because 12 has the prime factors 2 and 3, so the degree is 4. The primitive twelfth roots of unity are the roots of the fourth cyclotomic polynomial, and adjoining one of them to the rationals gives a degree four extension.
